scenario.summary: The Storm-2561 campaign uses SEO poisoning on search engines like Bing to direct users to lookalike VPN download sites. These sites harvest credentials through a multi-stage JavaScript prompt before delivering a legitimate, signed WatchGuard installer to avoid suspicion. Stolen credentials are then utilized for unauthorized access to external remote services.

meta.rationale: The hunt should start by identifying the hostnames of VPN gateways. If the organization uses cloud-native VPN services (e.g., AWS Client VPN), the device_hostname may be the service provider name. Focus on servers and high-privilege user accounts first.
meta.hypothesis: Adversaries are using credentials stolen from lookalike WatchGuard VPN download sites to authenticate to corporate VPNs from anomalous geographic regions or hosting provider IP space.

blind_spots.risk: If an attacker uses a residential proxy in the same country as the user, 'src_location_country' rarity will not trigger, potentially hiding the intrusion.

blind_spots.requires: Advanced IP reputation including residential ISP flagging
blind_spots.remediation: Integrate advanced IP reputation feeds that distinguish residential ISPs from commercial hosting providers.

hunt.name: Unauthorized VPN Access via Stolen WatchGuard Credentials
hunt.description: This hunt examines the identity plane for unauthorized VPN sessions that match the Storm-2561 phishing profile. It looks for successful authentications from rare countries or proxies, then fans out to correlate those sessions with potentially sensitive administrative actions in the cloud. By weighing the source rarity against the user's subsequent behavior, an agent can identify session hijacking or credential abuse that bypasses standard login rules. This hunt focuses on the initial access stage where stolen credentials are used to bypass the perimeter.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname, service_name, dst_endpoint_name FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (LOWER(service_name) LIKE '%vpn%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%vpn%' OR LOWER(logon_process_name) LIKE '%vpn%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify the hostnames and service names acting as VPN gateways to scope the subsequent behavioral analysis.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames reporting VPN-related authentication. Silence indicates no VPN logs matched the keywords.

primitive_config.label: Identify Active VPN Gateways
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname, service_name, dst_endpoint_name FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (LOWER(service_name) LIKE '%vpn%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%vpn%' OR LOWER(logon_process_name) LIKE '%vpn%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames reporting VPN-related authentication. Silence indicates no VPN logs matched the keywords.

config.content: SELECT src_location_country, src_location_city, is_proxy, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS user_count, COUNT(*) AS login_count FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE activity_id = 1 AND status_id = 1 AND (LOWER(service_name) LIKE '%vpn%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%vpn%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_location_country, src_location_city, is_proxy HAVING user_count <= 3
config.description: Stack-count VPN logins by country and city to identify successful authentications from locations that are statistically rare for the organization.
config.expected_signal: VPN logins from countries or cities with very few associated users. Large user counts indicate known regional offices or remote work hubs.

primitive_config.label: Rare VPN Source Locations
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_location_country, src_location_city, is_proxy, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS user_count, COUNT(*) AS login_count FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE activity_id = 1 AND status_id = 1 AND (LOWER(service_name) LIKE '%vpn%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%vpn%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_location_country, src_location_city, is_proxy HAVING user_count <= 3
primitive_config.expected: VPN logins from countries or cities with very few associated users. Large user counts indicate known regional offices or remote work hubs.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, api_operation, api_service_name, resource_name, status, time FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE activity_id IN (1, 3, 4) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify administrative or impactful cloud API operations that occurred after a user logged in, which may indicate an attacker using the session.
config.expected_signal: Create, Update, or Delete API calls. These are enriched for the analyst to correlate with rare VPN logins.

config.objective: Determine if any users exhibit anomalous VPN logins from rare countries or proxies that are immediately followed by significant cloud API changes (Create/Update/Delete).
config.description: Evaluate whether the VPN logins are unauthorized by correlating location rarity and subsequent cloud actions per user.
config.expected_signal: A per-host or per-user verdict indicating the likelihood of session compromise.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign for each user identified in the logins, citing specific IP and action rows.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one user account
config.condition: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one user account
config.description: Direct high-confidence compromises to containment and uncertain cases to manual analyst review.
Immediately terminate the suspected unauthorized access to prevent further damage.
config.instructions: Revoke all active sessions for the malicious user account and disable the account in the identity provider. Enforce a password reset and MFA re-enrollment.

config.description: Perform a deeper investigation into the user's activity to ensure no other internal resources were accessed.
config.instructions: Examine the internal traffic logs (e.g., hb_smb_activity) for the source IP associated with the suspicious VPN login. Confirm with the user if they were traveling or using a proxy.

config.description: Document findings and update any baselines or watchlists for future monitoring.
config.instructions: Record the number of false positives and update the organization's travel baseline if rare locations were found to be legitimate.
